The original definition of 'representative' means an employee or agent of an investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that adviser.

The 2020-amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' is broader, including any member, partner, officer, director, employee, or sales staff of the investment adviser engaged in providing investment advisory services, especially client-facing roles, excluding only clerical or administrative staff without client interaction.

Therefore, the 2020-amended definition covers a wider set of persons than the original definition of 'representative' within an investment advisory firm and they do not cover the same set of persons.

Explanation — All client-facing persons such as sales staff, service relationship managers, client relationship managers, etc., by whatever name called shall be deemed to be persons associated with investment advice, but do not include persons who discharge clerical or office administrative functions where there is no client interface.

## Hardship plans

A hardship plan reduces or suspends collection for an agreed period while the customer's
circumstances recover. An agent may apply one where all of the following hold:

escalated. Do not offer a hardship plan the customer has not asked for, and do not use one as a
substitute for escalating a case where the customer has described a change in circumstances that
this policy says a human must assess.

An agent may not move or amend a payment that is already scheduled; such a request must be escalated to a human.

citations.quote:
## Payments

An agent may schedule a **new** one-off payment against an active loan: due no earlier than today
and no more than **60 days** ahead, for an amount between **₹100** and **₹5,00,000**. A loan that
has been closed takes no further payments.

The servicing tooling cannot move, amend or cancel a payment that is already scheduled, and
scheduling a second payment does not replace the first — it creates a second obligation, and the
customer will be collected for both. So a request to *move* an existing instalment to a different
date is not something an agent may do by scheduling another payment. Verify the customer, tell
them plainly that the date cannot be changed automatically, and hand the case to a human. A
request to add a payment the customer does not already owe — a part payment, an extra payment —
is an ordinary scheduling request and needs no escalation.

The original version of Regulation 16(3) permitted withdrawal of a rating only if the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company.

The 2018-amended Regulation 16(3) added that withdrawal of a rating can also occur "as may be specified by the Board from time to time," expanding the grounds for withdrawal beyond the original criteria.

citations.quote:
Passage A:
Regulation 16(3) (pre-2018): A credit rating agency shall not withdraw a rating so long as the obligations under the security rated by it are outstanding, except where the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company.

Passage B:
Regulation 16(3) (as substituted w.e.f. 30-05-2018): A credit rating agency shall not withdraw a rating so long as the obligations under the security rated by it are outstanding, except where the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company, or as may be specified by the Board from time to time.

SEBI must give not less than ten days advance notice to an investment adviser before ordering an inspection under regulation 23 of SEBI IA Regulations, 2013.

SEBI can dispense with this advance notice if it is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given; in such cases, SEBI may direct by a written order that the inspection be conducted without notice.

citations.quote: Regulation 24(1): Before ordering an inspection under regulation 23, the Board shall give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-regulation (1), where the Board is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given, it may by an order in writing direct that the inspection of the affairs of the investment adviser be taken up without such notice.
